line: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 c4 Nb6 d4 d6 exd6 cxd6
teaches: When two recaptures are both sound, prefer the one that creates a structure with a plan built in — recapturing to leave majorities on opposite wings gives each side a clear job, and the whole middlegame plays itself by plan rather than by move-to-move invention.
explains: The pawns have traded so that the wing majorities point in opposite directions — the queenside pawns outnumber their counterparts and will advance there, while the opponent's extra kingside pawn does the same on the other wing. The imbalance is the plan: push where you are the majority.
structural: the recapture chosen for the structure it leaves — opposite majorities, each side owning one wing
